item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong sectoral outcome movement in macro stabilization and some service-delivery/inclusion programs.\nI did not find a clean, broad national indicator showing that ordinary living standards, security, and civic freedom improved together by year-end.\nThe evidence instead splits: economic indicators and some program outputs improved, while conflict, food access, detention, and civil-space indicators worsened or stayed highly negative.","evidence":[{"title":"The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: First Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-11-04","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/11/04/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-first-review-under-the-extended-credit-facility-557019","summary":"The IMF said Ethiopia’s reform program was advancing well, all quantitative performance criteria were met, four of five structural benchmarks were met, and the exchange-rate transition was narrowing the parallel-market gap.
